gaps.concept: Low estrogen causes vaginal atrophy: reduced glycogen and lactobacilli, elevated pH, parabasal cells, dryness, and dyspareunia.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes postmenopausal atrophy from infectious vaginitis in a patient with irritation and elevated vaginal pH.

gaps.concept: Bacterial vaginosis is polymicrobial anaerobic dysbiosis with little inflammation or leukocyte response.
gaps.why_tested: Explains thin discharge and clue cells without prominent vulvar inflammation.

gaps.concept: Vulvovaginal candidiasis causes intense pruritus and vulvar erythema, typically without a fishy odor.
gaps.why_tested: Separates candidiasis from bacterial vaginosis when the stem emphasizes itching and inflammation.

gaps.concept: Bartholin glands are mucus-secreting vestibular glands; abscesses are often polymicrobial, including enteric bacteria and anaerobes.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies the affected gland and likely microbiology of a painful unilateral vestibular mass.

gaps.concept: Lichen sclerosus often causes intense pruritus and a vulvar-perianal figure-eight pattern; biopsy shows epidermal atrophy and dermal sclerosis.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies lichen sclerosus from a pruritic white lesion or histologic specimen.

gaps.concept: High-potency topical corticosteroids are first-line treatment for vulvar lichen sclerosus.
gaps.why_tested: Tests the initial treatment of a characteristic pruritic white vulvar lesion.

gaps.concept: Erosive lichen planus can involve the vagina and cause erosions or scarring; lichen sclerosus generally spares vaginal mucosa.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes two inflammatory vulvar lesions when vaginal involvement is described.

gaps.concept: HPV-associated vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia is usually HPV-16–related, p16-positive, and shows squamous atypia without stromal invasion.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies a precancerous vulvar biopsy and separates it from invasive squamous carcinoma.

gaps.concept: Differentiated vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia is HPV-independent and often shows abnormal p53 staining.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes the precursor of HPV-negative vulvar carcinoma from HPV-associated vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia.

gaps.concept: Vulvar squamous carcinoma commonly spreads first to inguinal lymph nodes.
gaps.why_tested: Predicts regional nodal spread from an invasive vulvar lesion.

gaps.concept: Vulvar extramammary Paget disease typically appears as a chronic pruritic, eczematous red plaque.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies Paget disease from a persistent vulvar rash that resembles dermatitis.

gaps.concept: Condyloma acuminatum produces exophytic, cauliflower-like anogenital warts.
gaps.why_tested: Connects the visible lesion with the listed HPV types and koilocytes.

gaps.concept: Genital molluscum contagiosum causes umbilicated papules; biopsy shows large intracytoplasmic Henderson–Patterson inclusions.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes poxvirus papules from HPV warts on the vulva.

gaps.concept: Genital herpes causes painful grouped vesicles that rupture into ulcers; HSV-2 more commonly causes recurrent genital disease.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes herpes from other causes of genital ulcers.

gaps.concept: HSV cytology shows multinucleated giant cells with Cowdry type A inclusions; genital HSV establishes latency in sacral sensory ganglia.
gaps.why_tested: Links an ulcer specimen or recurrent episodes to HSV pathogenesis.

gaps.concept: Acyclovir and valacyclovir treat genital HSV; viral thymidine kinase activates acyclovir, which inhibits viral DNA polymerase.
gaps.why_tested: Tests the drug mechanism in a patient with recurrent painful genital vesicles.

gaps.concept: Primary syphilis causes a painless, indurated chancre with usually nontender regional lymphadenopathy.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes a syphilitic vulvar ulcer from painful herpes or chancroid.

gaps.concept: Secondary syphilis can cause broad, flat, moist condylomata lata, unlike exophytic HPV condylomata acuminata.
gaps.why_tested: Separates similarly named anogenital lesions caused by different pathogens.

gaps.concept: Syphilis is screened with RPR or VDRL and confirmed with treponemal testing; penicillin G is first-line treatment.
gaps.why_tested: Connects a characteristic genital lesion to its diagnostic tests and initial treatment.

gaps.concept: Haemophilus ducreyi causes chancroid: painful soft ulcers with ragged edges and tender suppurative inguinal nodes.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes chancroid from a painless syphilitic chancre.

gaps.concept: Chlamydia trachomatis L1–L3 causes lymphogranuloma venereum: a transient painless lesion followed by painful inguinal buboes.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies the organism from the sequence of a fleeting genital lesion and later lymphadenopathy.

gaps.concept: Klebsiella granulomatis causes donovanosis: painless beefy-red genital ulcers, usually without lymphadenopathy, with intracellular Donovan bodies.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes donovanosis from other ulcerative sexually transmitted infections.

gaps.concept: Chlamydia trachomatis or Neisseria gonorrhoeae cervicitis causes mucopurulent discharge and a friable cervix; nucleic acid amplification tests identify the pathogen.
gaps.why_tested: Separates cervical discharge from vaginitis in a reproductive-tract infection vignette.

gaps.concept: Vaginal upper two-thirds derives from Müllerian ducts; the lower third derives from urogenital sinus sinovaginal bulbs.
gaps.why_tested: Tests vaginal embryologic origin in a congenital-anomaly stem.

gaps.concept: A Gartner duct cyst is a remnant of the mesonephric, or Wolffian, duct.
gaps.why_tested: Asks the embryologic source of a lateral vaginal-wall cyst.

gaps.concept: Imperforate hymen from failed canalization causes primary amenorrhea, cyclic pelvic pain, hematocolpos, and a bulging bluish hymen.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies vaginal outflow obstruction in an adolescent with cyclic pain but no menses.

gaps.concept: DES-associated vaginal adenosis consists of glandular columnar epithelium replacing normal squamous mucosa and may appear as red granular patches.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies the precursor finding in a patient exposed to DES in utero.

gaps.concept: Sarcoma botryoides has a cambium layer of densely packed malignant cells immediately beneath the vaginal epithelium.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies the characteristic histology of a child's grape-like vaginal tumor.

gaps.concept: Primary vaginal squamous carcinoma is associated with high-risk HPV; vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia is its squamous precursor.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes primary HPV-related vaginal cancer from carcinoma extending from the cervix.
